copy.overviewTitle: A restaurant GST invoice starts with the right outlet profile.
copy.overviewParagraphOne: Restaurant GST billing software should reflect the restaurant’s actual registration and tax setup. In RestaBee, the outlet profile controls the document type and configured tax treatment used in the billing workflow. Tax profiles define the components and rates applied to menu items; the resulting bill preview shows the captured calculation for staff to review.
copy.overviewParagraphTwo: Restaurant registrations can follow different GST rules. Under regular registration, the applicable tax is calculated on the taxable supply and the invoice shows the required tax details. Where an eligible restaurant uses the composition scheme, the composition levy is a tax paid on turnover by the business. It is not a separate GST amount to add to each guest’s bill. RestaBee restaurant GST billing software distinguishes these setups in the invoice workflow so the selected document type matches the configured regime.
copy.regimeTitle: The 5% figure can describe two different calculations.
copy.regimeParagraphOne: For restaurant services away from specified premises, the CBIC rate schedule lists a 5% rate, split as 2.5% CGST and 2.5% SGST for an intra-state supply, subject to the notification’s conditions. That is tax on the supply under the regular route. Applicable rates and input tax credit treatment depend on the exact supply and business circumstances, so the outlet’s settings should follow advice from its tax professional.
copy.regimeParagraphTwo: The composition scheme is a separate route for businesses that are eligible and have opted into it. The composition rate shown in the rules is calculated on aggregate turnover. A composition taxpayer cannot collect GST separately from customers or issue a tax invoice for those supplies; the customer document is a bill of supply. GST billing software for restaurant teams should reflect that distinction in the bill type. The restaurant’s eligibility and obligations depend on current GST law, so the POS profile should be configured only after the registration status has been confirmed.
copy.invoiceTitle: A GST restaurant bill with the fields staff need to review.
copy.invoiceDescription: For a regular registration, the tax invoice layout can present supplier identity, invoice number and date, item or service description, taxable value and configured tax components. When a registered business customer requests a B2B invoice, staff can add that customer’s name, address, state and GSTIN to the invoice record. Required fields vary with the transaction and current rules, and the issuer remains responsible for confirming the document particulars before issue.
copy.thermalTitle: Review the bill before printing a thermal copy.
copy.thermalParagraphOne: RestaBee supports bill printing through a compatible printer configured for the chosen device and connection. A thermal print can carry the bill details generated by the configured invoice workflow, including the tax lines and customer identity captured for that bill. Printer model, paper width and connection method affect output, so check a test print during setup and make sure the text and totals are legible on the paper roll used at the outlet.
copy.thermalParagraphTwo: The outlet profile sets the configured tax treatment, and the printer reproduces the selected bill layout. Confirm whether the outlet uses regular registration or composition, check the document type and review the tax components before issue. For an intra-state supply, configured CGST and SGST lines can appear separately where the tax treatment calls for them. The place of supply and registered location determine the applicable tax components, so configure each outlet for its own registration and location. Restaurant GST billing software carries the reviewed values into the compatible print workflow.
copy.customerTitle: Capture GSTIN details for a business customer.
copy.customerParagraphOne: A registered customer may need a tax invoice with its GSTIN and registered details. RestaBee lets authorized staff enter customer name, phone, GSTIN, address and state for an invoice. Those details appear on the bill record when provided. The team can confirm the customer details with the requester before issuing the invoice, reducing corrections caused by incomplete billing information.
copy.customerParagraphTwo: Customer GSTIN fields support invoice preparation, while the restaurant’s tax adviser or portal confirms recipient eligibility and reporting requirements. For a registered customer, GST details for a restaurant bill should be confirmed before issue. Keep the final issued document with the outlet’s tax records for applicable return filing, e-invoicing and reconciliation processes.
copy.workflowTitle: From outlet tax setup to a reviewed bill.
copy.workflowDescription: Restaurant GST billing software keeps outlet identity, tax treatment, customer details and printing aligned. Staff review the bill’s values and document type before issuing it to the guest or business customer.
copy.scopeTitle: Configured tax display, with the right boundaries.
copy.scopeParagraphOne: RestaBee calculates bill tax from configured outlet and item profiles, captures tax components with the bill and supports printing on compatible setups. Restaurant GST billing software keeps these values in the order-to-bill record for staff review. The restaurant’s tax adviser and the relevant government portals handle registration eligibility, regime selection, return filing, e-way bills and e-invoices.
copy.scopeParagraphTwo: Owners should confirm the registration regime, rate, place-of-supply treatment, document requirements and printer layout with their accountant or tax adviser. After that review, the outlet profile can be configured and tested against representative orders before the team uses it for live billing. Revisit the setup when registrations or applicable rules change.
copy.sourceDescription: The notes above summarize official CBIC material and product behavior. Confirm current applicability with a qualified tax professional before changing outlet settings.

regimes.title: Regular GST registration
regimes.rateLabel: Applicable tax on the taxable supply
regimes.description: Configured tax profiles apply the approved treatment to items and show the captured tax components on the bill. The CBIC schedule currently lists 5% for restaurant service other than at specified premises, split 2.5% CGST and 2.5% SGST for intra-state supplies, with conditions. Confirm applicability and input tax credit treatment for the outlet.

regimes.title: Composition scheme
regimes.rateLabel: 5% composition levy on aggregate turnover, where applicable
regimes.description: The levy is paid by an eligible opted-in business on turnover. It is not GST collected separately from each customer. Composition taxpayers issue a bill of supply for these supplies and cannot issue a tax invoice or collect tax separately.

faqs.question: What does restaurant GST billing software do in RestaBee?
faqs.answer: It applies configured outlet and item tax profiles to bill calculations, presents the captured tax lines for review and keeps the issued document linked to its order and collections.

faqs.question: Is the 5% composition levy added to a guest’s restaurant bill?
faqs.answer: No. The composition levy is paid by an eligible opted-in business on aggregate turnover. A composition taxpayer cannot collect GST separately from customers for those supplies and issues a bill of supply.

faqs.question: How is regular GST different from composition billing?
faqs.answer: Regular registration applies the tax treatment relevant to the taxable supply and uses a tax invoice. Composition eligibility and levy work differently: tax is calculated on turnover by the business, and customer bills use a bill of supply. Confirm eligibility and current rules with a tax professional.

faqs.question: Can a restaurant GST invoice show CGST and SGST separately?
faqs.answer: For an intra-state supply where that treatment applies, configured tax components can be presented separately. The location and place-of-supply rules determine whether CGST and SGST or another treatment applies.

faqs.question: Can I add a business customer’s GSTIN to a restaurant bill?
faqs.answer: Authorized staff can enter the customer name, address, state and GSTIN for an invoice. The issuer should confirm the details and required invoice particulars before issue.

faqs.question: Can RestaBee print a GST bill on a thermal printer?
faqs.answer: RestaBee supports printing bills through compatible configured printers. Confirm the model, paper width, connection and sample output during setup.

faqs.question: Does RestaBee file GST returns or create e-invoices?
faqs.answer: RestaBee supports configured bill tax, invoice details and compatible printing. The restaurant’s tax adviser and relevant government portals handle return filing, e-invoices, e-way bills and reconciliation.

faqs.question: Who should configure the restaurant GST profile?
faqs.answer: The restaurant owner should confirm the registration regime, applicable rates, place of supply and document requirements with an accountant or tax adviser, then configure and test the outlet profile.
